messages.subject: problem with parboot or Nmix.gof.test with large simulation numbers
parts:
Hello everyone,

I want to use parboot or Nmix.gof.test  to perform a goodness of fit and collect c-hat values. 

Because I am comparing various univariate models and for various species, I am using as.formula and paste to build the formula for the pcount model. here an example: 


I selected one detection model from a list based on AICc, and then set the detection formula using

 if(paste(aicc_det$Modnames[1])=="det5"){{aux <- 'Ordinal_date' }}

 if(paste(aicc_det$Modnames[1])=="det6"){{aux <- 'river_sound ' }}


Then, to test the effect of various covariates in the abundance model I use:

det.form_1<- as.formula(paste("~", paste(aux), "~ log_connectivity40" ))

  det.form_2<- as.formula(paste("~", paste(aux), "~ -1 + Structural_connectivity" ))

  det.form_3<- as.formula(paste("~", paste(aux), "~ log_area" ))

 

 

Then, use the det.form character as the formula in the pcount function: 

 mod1<- pcount(det.form_1, umf, K=100, mixture='P')

mod2<- pcount(det.form_2, umf, K=100, mixture='P'),....etc

 

 

I want to use parboot or  Nmix.gof.test  to perform a goodness of fit for each of the models. 



If I use a small number of simulations there is no problem, I used:

gof.mod1 <- Nmix.gof.test(mod1, nsim=50)

 

> gof.mod1

Chi-square goodness-of-fit for N-mixture model of 'unmarkedFitPCount' class

Observed chi-square statistic = 156.9073 

Number of bootstrap samples = 50

P-value = 0.28

Quantiles of bootstrapped statistics:

  0%  25%  50%  75% 100% 

 114  138  151  158  205 

Estimate of c-hat = 1.05 

 

But If I increase the number of simulations, I run into the following error.

gof.mod1 <- Nmix.gof.test(mod1, nsim=100)

 

I get the following error: 

> gof.mod1 <- Nmix.gof.test(mod1, nsim=100)

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 

  7 nodes produced errors; first error: object 'det.form_1' not found

I tried the same using the parboot function and it produce the same error with simulations > 50. 

 

  fitstats <- function(mod1) {

    observed <- getY(mod1@data)

    expected <- fitted(mod1)

    resids <- residuals(mod1)

    sse <- sum(resids^2)

    chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)

    freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)

    out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)

    return(out)

  }

  

  (pb <- parboot(mod1, fitstats, nsim=100))




It sound that it is related with parallel processing (although I have not set the analysis to run in parallel), and the fact that I am using predefine argument in the formula of pcount.


I will much appreciate any hint or ideas to solve this problem


Isabel M Rojas

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] problem with parboot or Nmix.gof.test with large simulation numbers
parts:
Hi Isabel,


I would first try to debug by specifying your model the "classic way", e.g., 

 mod1<- pcount(~ 1 ~ log_connectivity40, umf, K=100, mixture='P')

to determine if it's either a problem with the data or the automated formulas you are building that are at the root of the problem.


What do you get when you specify mod1@formula? Both simulate and parboot (also used by Nmix.gof.test) use this info to run the model with new data. You might also want to try parboot(, parallel = FALSE).


Best,


Marc

Thank you for your suggestions, Marc. I tried them out and it solved the simulation problem.
I did encounter few other issues and so I am posing a couple of new questions below. Here is the report: 

 

Yes, I tried the simulation using the classical way to specify the model with a larger number of simulation and did not encounter the problem (that made me think about the problem with parallel processing).

 

I looked at the model formula, and it is the form that matches "det.form_1"

> mod1@formula
~Temp ~ log_connectivity40

 

Today, I tried to stop the parallel processing, and it worked using parboot(,parallel=FALSE)

 

It takes a bit longer. About 3 more minutes.

 

Question 1.

Since I will be running this test for various models and about 20 species, I wonder if there is a way to pass the argument (the automated formulas) to the multiple cores (My little understanding of this is that It may not be possible in a Window system, when using socket approach).

 

 

In addition, I encounter a new problem. I have unbalance data  (I am using 2 visits, but second visit only occurred in half of the sites).  Therefore, the fitstats function does not work because there are NA in the observed and resids arrays. While solving the other problems above, I trick the function to only use one visit:

 

 fitstats <- function(mod1) {

    observed <- getY(mod1@data)[,1]

    expected <- fitted(mod1)[,1]

    resids <- residuals(mod1)[,1]

sse <- sum(resids^2)

    chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)

    freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)

    out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)

    return(out)

  }

pb <- parboot(mod1, fitstats, nsim=500, parallel=FALSE)

 

And this worked ok.

 c_hat_estimate<- chisq/mean(p...@t.star[,2])

[1] 0.936256

 

In addition, I tried using both visit by changing the NA's to 0.

fitstats <- function(mod1) {

    observed <- getY(mod1@data)
observed[,2]<- sapply(observed[,2], function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x))

expected <- fitted(mod1)

    resids <- residuals(mod1)
resids[,2]<- sapply(resids[,2], function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x))

sse <- sum(resids^2)

    chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)

    freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)

    out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)

    return(out)

  }

pb <- parboot(mod1, fitstats, nsim=500, parallel=FALSE)

 

Call: parboot(object = mod1, statistic = fitstats, nsim = 500, parallel = FALSE)

Parametric Bootstrap Statistics:

freemanTukey  63.8           2.49             6.59        0.337

Chisq        107  133 152 161 175   202  246
freemanTukey  42   48  57  61  66    74   87

t_B = Vector of bootstrap samples

 

My estimated c-hat when using the data for both visits is:

 c_hat_estimate<- chisq/mean(p...@t.star[,2])

[1] 1.061092

 

Although Chisq, sse and freemanTukey are higher when using both visit, I observed that both approached lead to similar c-hat.

 

Question 2.

I wonder what would be the best approach here. I am not quite convince that changing the NA's is the best way to go because I am assuming that those sites I did not visit had an observed count of 0 (which explain the increase in Chisq, etc).

In the other hand, I wonder if testing the fit of the model only one visit is OK.

How does  Nmix.gof.fit address this?  I was able to run that function with both visit. I am not sure how the function make use of the unbalance data. 

 

Thanks again for your super helpful suggestions.

Isabel

Hi Isabel,


for passing arguments to multiple cores for parallel processing, others might want to chime in.


I would definitely include both visits to assess the fit of your model, even if some sites only have 1 visit. The missing data on the second occasion, do not contribute to the chi-square. This corresponds to your approach of zeroing the NA's (for missed visits) in your fit statistics. This is also the route taken by Nmix.gof.test( ).


Hope it helps,

Marc

Hi Isabel,

Give the development version of unmarked a try on your models using formula objects.

install.packages("devtools") # If necessary
devtools::install_github("rbchan/unmarked")

Here's an example that demonstrates how it should work when passing a formula argument:

library(unmarked)
data(mallard)
mallardUMF <- unmarkedFramePCount(mallard.y, siteCovs = mallard.site,
                                  obsCovs = mallard.obs)
(form.obj <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(c("ivel", "date"), collapse = "+"), 
                             "~", paste(c("length", "elev", "forest"), collapse = "+"))))
(m1 <- pcount(~ ivel + date ~ length + elev + forest, mallardUMF, K=30)))
(m2 <- pcount(form.obj, mallardUMF, K=30))

p1 <- parboot(m1, nsim = 100, seed = 42, report = 5)
p2 <- parboot(m2, nsim = 100, seed = 42, report = 5)
identical(p...@t.star, p...@t.star)

Let me know if you encounter any issues...

Best,
Adam
